notes.title: Update Version 0.2.1.0 New AI Is Here!
notes.content:
[h1]Update Notes For 0.2.1.0[/h1]

[b]-Complete re-write of the AI[/b]

[b]-Weather effects now transition into full effect[/b]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed Bug: Attack animation would not show above foundations
[*]Fixed Bug: Crafting the Hide Cap would give you Hide Armor instead
[*]Fixed Bug: Deconstruction table had issues, I fixed them
[*]Fixed Bug: Deconstruction tables were not saving their inventories
[*]Changed the name of "Hide Mk1" to "Hide Armor Mk1"[/list]

Hit [i]F3[/i] to view cool debugging info about the AI (it displays around the animals).

[h1]Finally... Decent AI[/h1]
Yes it is here at last and I am sick of coding AI now. It has been a constant struggle to make the pathing work while not destroying the framerate. I use A* pathing but you can only go so far when you have to navigate in a dynamic sandbox environment. As far as I have tested there are no major bugs with the new AI but please report it if you come by any while playing.

[h1]So What's Next?[/h1]
Multiplayer is probably the next step for me. I have over a month of work to put into I'm sure. I guess we'll see. In the meantime I will do my best to keep pushing out content updates and bug fixes. I hate to keep you all waiting but I promise it's not far. ːCuteBearDollː

notes.title: Big Update 0.2.0.0 (Please Read!)
notes.content:
[h1]What Took You So Long?![/h1]
I know! I'm so sorry about the delay. It wasn't supposed to take this long but there were a few bumps along the way. Read the story at the bottom of this announcement as it explains it all.


[h1]Update Notes For 0.2.0.0[/h1]

[b]New Implementations[/b]
[list][*]Implemented single building ceiling view (not all ceilings are transparent when indoors)
[*]Implemented pop-up UI for doors
[*]Implemented chunk generation checking for edge of the map to prevent generating structures in the water
[*]Implemented the ability to right click with items equipped in the hotbar to use
[*]Implemented UI for fishing
[*]Implemented drinking directly from ponds/lakes
[*]Implemented asynchronous auto-saving
[*]Implemented status updates for health
[*]Implemented status updates for insanity
[*]Implemented various environment detail objects
[*]Implemented Steam custom screenshot keys
[*]Implemented indoors check system for objects to prevent them rendering when the player is outside
[*]Implemented pop-up UI for deconstruction table
[*]Implemented 'Game Settings' menu
[*]Implemented health regeneration
[*]Implemented new tree system[/list]

[b]Major Changes[/b]
[list][*]Leaves can now be collected from various plants
[*]Leaves can now be used to fuel fires
[*]Added New Achievement: How To Get An Achievement
[*]Added New Passive: Sickness
[*]Added New Biome: Village (1 Chunk)
[*]Dropped items are now removed from the world after 5 minutes[/list]

[b]Minor Changes[/b]
[list][*]Decreased chance of desert biome expanding during world generation
[*]Cleaned up code around chunk generation (good for me, no difference for users)
[*]Lowered sanity reduction of Teddy Bear to 15%
[*]Doors can now be used with the custom interaction keys
[*]Sand will now always appear under ocean water
[*]Bandages now return 2 cloth in the deconstruction table
[*]All status updates have been changed to a second person point of view
[*]Reduced brightness of large fire
[*]Removed burn damage from fires
[*]Extremely high temperatures now affect health
[*]Lower damage done by dust storms by 50%
[*]Reduced loss of hunger, thirst, and sanity
[*]Changed fishing controls, 'right mouse button' is used now instead of the interaction key[/list]

[b]New Items[/b]
[list][*]Added New Item: Leaf
[*]Added New Item: Red Berries
[*]Added New Item: "The Haze"
[*]Added New Item: "Camo's Ham"
[*]Added New Item: "My Dear Pepe"
[*]Added New Item: "How To Get An Achievement"[/list]

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list][*]Optimizations made to 3D foundation/ceiling rendering
[*]Improved stability of various scripts
[*]Optimized dust storms
[*]Optimized insanity effects (clouds and creature particles)
[*]Optimized world generation of structures when looking for trees and rocks within the structure
[*]Water object has been extremely optimized
[*]Improved stability of saved games (No crashes yet)[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed Bug: When deconstructing items, items left in the output slot are deleted instead of ejected
[*]Fixed Bug: Fires could not be ignited during dust storms
[*]Fixed Bug: Various crops returned double the seeds before they are finished growing
[*]Fixed Bug: Ceilings could be placed without supports
[*]Fixed Bug: Weather status updates would only appear once
[*]Fixed Bug: Dropped items would not be deleted when in the water
[*]Fixed Bug: When loading saved games in slots farther in the list than slot 1, loads would not work
[*]Fixed Bug: Various objects spawn in the ocean
[*]Fixed Bug: Ocean water no longer overlaps strangely
[*]Fixed Bug: Items get deleted at the border of  water
[*]Fixed Bug: Doors can no longer be placed on top of other doors
[*]Fixed Bug: Upgrading constructed walls to stone walls did not cost anything
[*]Fixed Bug: Trees and rocks would spawn inside of structures[/list]


[h1]The Good News[/h1]
The update is stable from what I've tested and has tons of bug fixes as well as new content which can be found above. I recommend reading through it as many things have been changed.

[h1]The Bad News[/h1]
There has been a few missed due dates as I'm sure you have seen if you read these posts regularly. Starting with the multiplayer and such. I'd like to be open with everyone and explain my mistake, and what exactly happened.

[h1]A Series Of Unfortunate Events[/h1]
This all started back when I first got a new friend request on Steam from someone I didn't know. When most people add me I accept it which is what happened. We spoke for a bit. I discovered he was a programmer and he seemed very talented (which he is by the way) so I offered him a role on the team. I really wanted someone to take over the multiplayer so that I could focus on content and polishing for the time being.

It started with a due date that was missed by a few weeks. Eventually he told me he wanted to do the AI as a way to sort of take a break from the multiplayer work as it is pretty tedious. We set the due date 08/20/2015. That day passes and the AI is no where near ready. The release date for this update was supposed to be 08/24/2015. This obviously was an issue.

Spike (co-programmer) and I had a discussion involving his position as a co-programmer. We came to a healthy and reasonable conclusion. We are still friends and there are no hurt feelings. He had over scheduled himself and kept doing so until eventually it fell apart. He is no longer working on this game though. I also removed Idiotekque as a developer since his work was contract based and has not been called upon for a number of months.

[h1]What I've Have Learned[/h1]
I'm going to be working solo from now on. I don't like relying on people. It isn't a good practice when you can do it yourself anyways. Maybe down the road if I were to own a company but right now it simply is easier to do things myself. From now on I will be the only developer for Project Explore. I may reach out for art from a few friends occasionally but that's about it.

[h1]So What's Next?[/h1]
I am going to be re-writing the AI next since that was the plan for this update. I don't break promises. It just isn't in me to do so. Though to be honest with everyone I can not set a really solid due date on the next update since I have a few things to tackle over the next couple weeks. I will be working around the clock once again so we'll see what happens!

Until next time, fare well! ːCuteBearDollː

"My Dear Pepe"

[*]Implemented indoors check system for objects to prevent them rendering when the player is outside
[*]Implemented pop-up UI for deconstruction table
[*]Implemented 'Game Settings' menu
[*]Implemented health regeneration
[*]Implemented new tree system[/list]

[b]Major Changes[/b]
[list][*]Leaves can now be collected from various plants
[*]Leaves can now be used to fuel fires
[*]Added New Achievement: How To Get An Achievement
[*]Added New Passive: Sickness
[*]Added New Biome: Village (1 Chunk)
[*]Dropped items are now removed from the world after 5 minutes[/list]

[b]Minor Changes[/b]
[list][*]Decreased chance of desert biome expanding during world generation
[*]Cleaned up code around chunk generation (good for me, no difference for users)
[*]Lowered sanity reduction of Teddy Bear to 15%
[*]Doors can now be used with the custom interaction keys
[*]Sand will now always appear under ocean water
[*]Bandages now return 2 cloth in the deconstruction table
[*]All status updates have been changed to a second person point of view
[*]Reduced brightness of large fire
[*]Removed burn damage from fires
[*]Extremely high temperatures now affect health
[*]Lower damage done by dust storms by 50%
[*]Reduced loss of hunger, thirst, and sanity
[*]Changed fishing controls, 'right mouse button' is used now instead of the interaction key[/list]

[b]New Items[/b]
[list][*]Added New Item: Leaf
[*]Added New Item: Red Berries
[*]Added New Item: "The Haze"
[*]Added New Item: "Camo's Ham"
[*]Added New Item: "My Dear Pepe"
[*]Added New Item: "How To Get An Achievement"[/list]

[b]Optimizations[/b]
[list][*]Optimizations made to 3D foundation/ceiling rendering
[*]Improved stability of various scripts
[*]Optimized dust storms
[*]Optimized insanity effects (clouds and creature particles)
[*]Optimized world generation of structures when looking for trees and rocks within the structure
[*]Water object has been extremely optimized
[*]Improved stability of saved games (No crashes yet)[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed Bug: When deconstructing items, items left in the output slot are deleted instead of ejected
[*]Fixed Bug: Fires could not be ignited during dust storms
[*]Fixed Bug: Various crops returned double the seeds before they are finished growing
[*]Fixed Bug: Ceilings could be placed without supports
[*]Fixed Bug: Weather status updates would only appear once
[*]Fixed Bug: Dropped items would not be deleted when in the water
[*]Fixed Bug: When loading saved games in slots farther in the list than slot 1, loads would not work
[*]Fixed Bug: Various objects spawn in the ocean
[*]Fixed Bug: Ocean water no longer overlaps strangely
[*]Fixed Bug: Items get deleted at the border of  water
[*]Fixed Bug: Doors can no longer be placed on top of other doors
[*]Fixed Bug: Upgrading constructed walls to stone walls did not cost anything
[*]Fixed Bug: Trees and rocks would spawn inside of structures[/list]


[h1]The Good News[/h1]
The update is stable from what I've tested and has tons of bug fixes as well as new content which can be found above. I recommend reading through it as many things have been changed.

[h1]The Bad News[/h1]
There has been a few missed due dates as I'm sure you have seen if you read these posts regularly. Starting with the multiplayer and such. I'd like to be open with everyone and explain my mistake, and what exactly happened.

[h1]A Series Of Unfortunate Events[/h1]
This all started back when I first got a new friend request on Steam from someone I didn't know. When most people add me I accept it which is what happened. We spoke for a bit. I discovered he was a programmer and he seemed very talented (which he is by the way) so I offered him a role on the team. I really wanted someone to take over the multiplayer so that I could focus on content and polishing for the time being.

It started with a due date that was missed by a few weeks. Eventually he told me he wanted to do the AI as a way to sort of take a break from the multiplayer work as it is pretty tedious. We set the due date 08/20/2015. That day passes and the AI is no where near ready. The release date for this update was supposed to be 08/24/2015. This obviously was an issue.

Spike (co-programmer) and I had a discussion involving his position as a co-programmer. We came to a healthy and reasonable conclusion. We are still friends and there are no hurt feelings. He had over scheduled himself and kept doing so until eventually it fell apart. He is no longer working on this game though. I also removed Idiotekque as a developer since his work was contract based and has not been called upon for a number of months.

[h1]What I've Have Learned[/h1]
I'm going to be working solo from now on. I don't like relying on people. It isn't a good practice when you can do it yourself anyways. Maybe down the road if I were to own a company but right now it simply is easier to do things myself. From now on I will be the only developer for Project Explore. I may reach out for art from a few friends occasionally but that's about it.

[h1]So What's Next?[/h1]
I am going to be re-writing the AI next since that was the plan for this update. I don't break promises. It just isn't in me to do so. Though to be honest with everyone I can not set a really solid due date on the next update since I have a few things to tackle over the next couple weeks. I will be working around the clock once again so we'll see what happens!

Until next time, fare well! :CuteBearDoll:

"My Dear Pepe"

notes.title: Taking The Time To Make Big Changes
notes.content:
Let me start off by saying that the next update is going to take about two weeks to develop and bug test before release. There is a lot more going on in this update in comparison to others. I've made changes to a lot of the game's base code such as rendering of certain objects and the chunk system.

[h1][b]New NPC System[/b][/h1]
The largest upcoming feature is the NPC re-write. Now it's important to keep in mind that this is not my department of work; Spike (co-programmer) is taking this on himself so I am not able to speak for its exact due date but we estimate it will be done hopefully around the 24th of this month.

[h1][b]Making The World Less Empty[/b][/h1]
I've listened to the community and have heard from a lot of people that the environment feels empty. The world just doesn't feel very lively. I am in the process of adding more plants and various world details.

[img=http://i.imgur.com/DVGwtt6.png]No environmental detail[/img]

[img=http://i.imgur.com/mZYOtKa.png]The two plants I've added so far[/img]

[h1][b]Village Biome[/b][/h1]
The houses randomly placed throughout the world is strange and really is only there to help in terms of gameplay. I love finding loot in games. You feel accomplished and every treasure you find is another exciting moment. So, I have been working on implementing a village biome. To clarify there will be no sort of civilization in these villages but there will be roads and houses.

[img=http://i.imgur.com/B66DRoC.png][/img]

I spent about 10 hours yesterday setting up this single village layout. Before the update is released I'm hoping to have about three different village biomes. Each one has multiple variations that can affect the roads, the houses, and the crates. The reason these take so long is because I have to handcraft these in code and then account for each possible result.

[h1][b]News On The Multiplayer[/b][/h1]
I want multiplayer to be a good experience from the beginning. With the silly NPCs we have now and the lack of a believable world I feel that anyone who picks up the game simply for the multiplayer would be left very disappointed. The game is lacking content and surface level appeal. I wanted from the beginning to create an awesome game that would stand out from others. I would be violating my own personal guidelines if I released multiplayer with the game in its current state. I can not make any promises as to when the multiplayer will be available but I can tell you that it is our next priority after this big update.

[h1][b]Live Updates On Our Progress[/b][/h1]
There is this awesome website called Trello that we use to show our development progress. I recommend giving it a look. It's pretty cool to see changes being made in realtime.

Link: [url=https://trello.com/b/eaw5bXk9/project-explore-alpha-0-2]https://trello.com/b/eaw5bXk9/project-explore-alpha-0-2[/url]

This doesn't in any way benefit us outside of helping us stay organized and providing the public with realtime information as to what will be in the next update. You are able to leave comments and vote for various cards. It's a good way to show what features you want most and what changes you think should be made.

Thanks to everyone for all the support! Best wishes and have a spectacular day!

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.5.6 Thirst, New Menu/UI, And Major Optimizations
notes.content:
[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.5.6[/h1]
[b]New Implementations[/b]
[list]
[*]Implemented audio loading system for music tracks and ambience (lowered CPU usage but increased memory usage, no longer reads from hard drive, also keeps less audio files in memory at a time)
[*]Implemented loading system for menu images (reduced memory usage by about 50 MB)
[*]Implemented mouse prompt UI system for the following items: Small Crate, Large Crate, Wood Table, and the Wood Chest
[*]Re-implemented Spike's world file compression script (please post in the forums if this leads to unstable saved games)
[*]Implemented thirst[/list]

[b]Minor Changes[/b]
[list][*]Added more to the game wiki (new items and updated some olds)
[*]'Food' stat in the inventory screen is now displayed as 'Hunger'
[*]Decreased hunger rate
[*]All liquid items now restore various amounts of thirst
[*]Made day/night lighting more visible
[*]Dust storms increase thirst rate
[*]Heartbeat sound effects are now a part of the volume system
[*]Ambient sounds now work correctly and play depending on the time of day
[*]Main menu says 'Hello' to you now[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed: Various possible future issues with the save file that needed to be fixed
[*]Fixed Bug: When loading a saved game in which a weather effect was active, ambient sounds would not play
[*]Fixed Bug: Saved games sometimes would experience buggy weather due to a messed up buffer data type
[*]Fixed Bug: Ambient sound playing at world start
[*]Fixed Bug: Possible crash involved with the wood chest[/list]

[b]New Artwork[/b]
[list][*]New Artwork: Main Menu (Gazelle)
[*]New Artwork: HUD (Gazelle)
[*]New Artwork: Time Of Day Clock (Gazelle)[/list]

[h1][b]The New UI And Main Menu[/b][/h1]
Gazelle (the other half of Seabass And Gazelle Studios) and I decided it was about time we did something about the shabby UI and main menu I had done so long ago. You see Gazelle has never contributed to the development of this game which is why she isn't listed as a developer. She did some wonderful artwork for the game now and it looks fantastic.


[img=http://i.imgur.com/67SeONn.png][/img]

[img=http://i.imgur.com/t4uHjcC.png][/img]

[img=http://i.imgur.com/8dBfglw.png][/img]


[h1][b]Big Optimizations[/b][/h1]
The music and ambience in Project Explore plays a big role in creating a mood and atmosphere for the game. It also was a big contributor to CPU/Hard disk usage. I never really took the time to make a loading/unloading system since I didn't see much reason to but since I plan on adding more music and additional audio in general it just makes sense to take care of it now.

I have implemented a system to load and unload audio as needed. You may notice that the game takes nearly 80 Mb of additional memory compared to before. This is because whichever music and ambient track is current playing is kept completely uncompressed in memory so that the CPU can stream it without any real usage. When these files are being used the game will unload all othe ambient and music tracks to reduce memory usage.

The main menu images including the splash art in the background are unloaded from memory as well once the game is launched. It only saved about 10 Mb but who cares. That might make it game playable for one more person.

[h1][b]Thirst, Making Survival A Bit More Difficult[/b][/h1]
Playing the game for even 30 minutes makes you start to crave a bit more of a challenge. Thirst is here and while it will not fill in the gap that is there it will help a bit. All liquid items replenish thirst now so I recommend finding a bottle quickly and living near lakes or ponds. Thirst is like hunger in the sense that if you let it reach zero you will start to lose heatlh. Thirst is affected by temperature like hunger is but will run down a bit faster. Dust storms will also decrease your thirst faster than usual.

[h1][b]Spike's World Compression Script[/b][/h1]
My wonderful co-programmer Spike wrote a script to compress the world into a much smaller size when saving a while ago but for quite some time there were issues with the save file I was using that was leading to misaligned and corrupt worlds. I believe I have finally fixed it after about an hour of non-stop save, quit, and load testing. While normally I don't see a huge advantage to saving 4 Mb of space for all this hassle there is a MASSIVE difference when it comes to larger worlds.

An 'Extra Large' world takes 64 Mb of space when saved in the default uncompressed format. With Spike's compression script that file is 4 Mb. That's a big difference. One worth all the hassle. So please post in the community discussion bug report section if you have any problems with the new save files. It is important to note that old saves WILL NOT work with this version.




Thanks for reading! Have an amazing day!

[b]OLDER SAVED GAMES WILL NOT WORK WITH THIS VERSION[/b]

[*]Changed Heavy Rain effect to rain a LOT more
[*]Lowered growth rate of all crops[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed Bug: Rain drops would fall through ceilings[/list]

[b]New Items[/b]
[list][*]Added New Item: Wood Photo Frame
[*]Added New Item: Wood Wash Board
[*]Added New Item: Towel
[*]Added New Item: Small Bag
[*]Added New Item: Blue Sock
[*]Added New Item: Red Sock
[*]Added New Item: Cloth Headwrap (Wearable)[/list]

[h1][b]New Weather, Dust Storms[/b][/h1]
Weather is a key part of the survival experience and something I have been putting off for some time. Rain only affects the game in two aspects: it's pretty and it makes crops grow faster. Not really all that exciting or game changing. Well now we have dust storms. A very different type of weather that can actually kill you.

There is a number of ways to survive which include hiding indoors or wearing a headwrap. As you probably know... inhaling massive amounts of dirt/dust isn't exactly a good way of staying in shape. The weather makes sense considering the surrounding desert biomes and nearby ocean. I think the dust storm adds a whole new challenge to the game and will help expand the gameplay further.

[h1][b]New Items (Explained)[/b][/h1]
You may have noticed the addition of seemingly useless items in Project Explore. Well they aren't useless! In fact no items are entirely useless. All 'useless' items can be deconstructed into cloth, strings, sticks, and other useful resources using a deconstruction table. One not so useless item I've added is the cloth headwrap (read more in the previous paragraph above).

[h1][b]News Regarding The Next Major Update[/b][/h1]
Until we release the multiplayer and AI re-write we have promised... I will continue to push these minor updates to help expand the game and hopefully get some user feedback about new features.

Thanks for reading and have a excellent day!

notes.title: The Next Major Update Information
notes.content:
[h1][b]So When Is The Next Update?[/b][/h1]

I'm not a huge fan of Early Access games that go off the radar for weeks at a time but I think it is important that I remain open and honest with everyone.

Spike (co-programmer) will be hard at work implementing multiplayer over the next 3 weeks and so that is our release date estimate (July 24th, 2015). Meanwhile I am working on implementing touch screen support for Windows Devices (except the phone, sorry, not a fan of the Windows phone). I may even be bringing Project Explore to the Android at some point but we'll have to see how that goes.

[h1][b]Explaining The Huge Delay[/b][/h1]

Multiplayer isn't something that can implemented over night. It's just not that simple. We are actually doing a entire seperate dedicated server that we will be distributing with the game as well as a master server. Anyone will be able to host their own server as a public server for anyone in the community to join via the server browser. We are going to do everything we can to support as many players as possible. The server is written in C# instead of Game Maker for the best possible performance. Of course you will need a decent bandwidth to handle lots of players but you shouldn't need a powerhouse PC just to host a small server.

I'll post again in another week or two with a status update to keep everyone informed and up to date with what is happening with Project Explore.

Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.5.4 No More Loading Chunks, Larger Worlds, More Items In The World!
notes.content:
[b]OLD SAVES DEFINITELY DO NOT WORK WITH THIS VERSION AND UP[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.5.4[/h1]
[b]New Implementations[/b]
[list][*]Chunk system re-write (chunk loading is now 190% faster)
[*]Implemented new item lists into world spawn (chests and skeletons now have updated item lists)
[*]Useless item list added to world item spawn (wallet, rag, etc)
[*]Re-implemented 'Large' world size
[*]Implemented new world size: Extra Large
[*]Item viewer can now be closed by pressing 'Escape' key[/list]

[b]New Items[/b]
[list][*]Added new item: Pencil[/list]

[b]Minor Changes[/b]
[list][*]Re-wrote screen pause script (faster pausing)
[*]Changed all surface item stack limits to 16 instead of 8
[*]Minor text changes to the item, 'Wood Log' which is now named 'Wood'
[*]Minor text changes to the item, 'Stick'
[*]Removed bloom shaders (pixel shader 2.0 is now supported again)
[*]Made 'Pencil' deconstructable[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed bug: Stalker and ripper kills were not kept when loading a saved game
[*]Fixed bug: Fish couldn't be cooked[/list]

[h1][b]New Chunk System (No More Lag)[/b][/h1]
You know how the game would hang when you stepped into a new chunk? Yeah, I fixed that. The world size can be just about any size you want now. I even added an 'Extra Large' option which is 120x120 chunks. In terms of screenspace, that is 153600*153600 pixels of world space. It's pretty massive. The best part is that the world is seamless. There is no lag at all. Start a world, let it load, after that it's smooth the whole way.

[h1][b]Working On Touch Screen Support (Thanks Intel!)[/b][/h1]
An Intel representative contacted me a month back or so and offered to send me a 2-1 laptop/tablet to help me develop Project Explore for the free form device (touch screen and such). I was blown away by the offer and accepted it of course. I received the device yesterday and got onscreen and multi-touch controls working. It's not polished and no where near ready but I just thought I'd mention it to everyone. I'll be adding a tablet mode option for those of you that wish to survive from the comfort of your bed.

Thanks for reading!

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.5.3 Smooth Day And Night Cycles, Enhanced Shaders, Death Screen, And So Much More!
notes.content:
[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.5.3[/h1]
[b]New Implementations[/b]
[list][*]Implemented death screen for singleplayer
[*]Implemented smooth ambient light transitions
[*]Implemented light bloom shader
[*]Made major enhancements to shaders
[*]Implemented heart beat effect (When the players health is below 25)
[*]Implemented 'Escape' key for backing through main menus[/list]

[b]Minor Changes[/b]
[list][*]Backing out of the graphics menu will now apply any changes you made
[*]Reduced the rate that fires burn through wood
[*]Made deer and bear meat cook-able now
[*]Lowered drop rates of crops
[*]Increased rate of food item spawns throughout the world
[*]Increased cost of wood for storage items
[*]Improved UI for cooking (big fire)
[*]Crafting string now gives you 2 strings instead of 1 (1 Cloth = 2 Strings)
[*]Changed the stats for fish items (reduced food and health)
[*]Removed 'Raw Wolf Meat' from world item spawn list
[*]Changed graphic option 'vignette shader' to 'shaders'
[*]Added 'Game Wiki' button to the main menu
[*]All fish can now be cooked[/list]

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
[list][*]Fixed bug: When setting a waypoint with the compass, your character would freeze outside of the UI afterwards
[*]Fixed bug: Compass waypoint list displaying a huge list of 'undefined' points
[*]Fixed bug: When using the deconstruction table on a stack of an item, it will consume the stack but only give a single drop
[*]Fixed bug: Surfaces can be placed on grass and sand
[*]Fixed bug: Ceilings are popping in and out in a strange manner.
[*]Fixed bug: Fire sound starts when clicked regardless of whether the fire starts or not
[*]Fixed bug: 'Light Up The Night' achievement could be completed by crafting a large crate
[*]Fixed bug: Crops return multiple seeds before final stage of growth when destroyed
[*]Fixed bug: Lantern would crash a saved game once loaded (occasionally)[/list]

[b]New Items[/b]
[list][*]Added new item: Cooked Trout
[*]Added new item: Cooked Seabass
[*]Added new item: Cooked Pink Salmon
[*]Added new item: Cooked Halibut[/list]

[b]New Artwork[/b]
[list][*]Updated steam icon artwork with new logo/icon
[*]Updated artwork: Tomato seeds
[*]Updated artwork: Corn Seeds
[*]Updated artwork: Potato
[*]Updated artwork: Corn
[*]Updated artwork: Seabass, Trout, Pink Salmon, and Halibut (All The Fish)[/list]

[h1][b]Beautiful Shaders And Day/Night Cycles[/b][/h1]
This update brings with it... TONS of eye candy. I've finally managed to work in a smooth day and night cycle. No more sudden lighting changes. Shaders are another thing I wanted to improve further for the users with stronger hardware. I know the first thing I do when I start up a game is go into the graphics menu and turn everything to the highest settings. I've made sure not to leave out those of you with older hardware/laptops. You can enable all the same features and get equal performance by simply disabling the shaders.

[h1][b]Some Major Bug Fixes[/b][/h1]
I found some pretty game breaking issues during 30 minute play session of Project Explore. For instance, the lantern would literally crash the game when you reloaded your save. Another example, the surface tiles you can place could be placed on grass and sand which was NEVER supposed to happen. Crops were super BROKEN and I didn't even notice until last night. The compass would freeze your player after you selected a waypoint. SO many issues that I was unaware of until now. 

I've done my best to make the game more playable. I realize I haven't been releasing the most stable updates recently but I'm doing by best here to make up for it. The only new feature I'm somewhat concerned about (concerned it may be unstable) is the death screen I added. I've tested it in multiple resolutions and windowed/full screen mode and it works correctly. But like most new features I probably overlooked something.

[h1][b]That's It For Now![/b][/h1]
Until next time... Thanks for reading and spread the word about Project Explore with all your friends! We really need your help in expanding our community. It'll make the multiplayer 10 times more fun with more people to experience it with.

[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.5.2 Cooking, New UIs, and More Shaders!
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.5.2[/h1]
[list][*]Implemented new interaction menu UI for various objects (small fire, big fire, lantern, forging table)
[*]Implemented cooking (small fire and big fire)
[*]Implemented brightness/contrast shader
[*]Implemented debug console (for developer use)
[*]Fixed bug: Various objects such as the small crate and lantern respawn after a saved game is loaded
[*]Fixed bug: After a game is loaded, buried animals appear where their grave is
[*]Fixed bug: Terrain surface doesn't update when you dig up or place a surface
[*]Fixed bug: When consumed the 'Honey Bar' item would display +10 hp but there was a gain of +20 hp. It now displays the correct amount
[*]Fixed bug: When player dies, music keeps playing
[*]Fixed bug: Wood walls crashing the game when placed
[*]Fixed the spelling of the word 'Caffeine' in multiple instances where it was spelled 'Caffine'
[*]Increased rate of sanity loss at night
[*]The world now becomes slightly darker when it rains (with the vignette shader enabled)
[*]Changed forging table to use the same system as the cooking (independent of UI)
[*]Changed the description of running/jogging shoes to make a bit more sense
[*]Modified the lighting effects of the small and big fires (Looks a bit better and brighter)
[*]Renamed item: 'Wolf Meat' is now 'Raw Wolf Meat'
[*]Renamed item: 'Bear Meat' is now 'Raw Bear Meat'
[*]Renamed item: 'Buck Meat' is now 'Raw Deer Meat'
[*]Removed item: Dull Knife
[*]Removed item: Sharp Knife
[*]Added new item: Broken Clock
[*]Added new item: Gear
[*]Added new item: Wallet
[*]Added new item: Rag
[*]Added new item: Cooked Wolf Meat
[*]Added new item: Cooked Bear Meat
[*]Added new item: Cooked Deer Meat
[*]New deconstruction items: Wallet, Rag, and Clock
[*]Updated artwork for 'Seabass (Fish)'
[*]The chance of precipitation has increased by 3.5%~
[*]Lowered the rate that crops grow at
[*]Removed 'Large' map option from the menu (Too many complaints of frame dipping and other issues)[/list]

[h1][b]Cooking... WHAT TOOK YOU SO LONG?!!?![/b][/h1]
The time has finally come and cooking has been implemented. This is something that was suggested to me by maybe 250 people, which is a lot obviously. I want to make sure Project Explore isn't a grind every step of the way but instead a smooth climb.

Anyhow cooking is in and fully functional. I've made sure to test it out vigorously to avoid releasing a bug filled update. I had to figure out a new UI for the camp fires to make this cooking system work and along the way decided that I may as well change the UI system for a couple of things. This list includes the furnace, lantern, small fire, and large fire. It's a similar UI to the way the hammer is handled.

I hope everyone enjoys this change and that it brings a much needed bit of realism/content to the game.

[h1][b]The Wiki/Website Is Still Being Worked On[/b][/h1]
We finally decided it was time to get a decent website url so I took the time to grab the domain 'projectexploregame.com' before someone else did. The wiki can still be accessed through my studio website but it can now also be accessed via our new domain. Our main website is not set up yet but it will be soon.

I've filled out a lot more items in the wiki which may prove useful to anyone who isn't sure on a specific item or how to use it.

The new website URL is as follows:
[url=http://wiki.projectexploregame.com/]Project Explore Wiki[/url]

I appreciate all the bug reports and suggestions recently. The community has been very helpful in the development of this game and I'm thankful that we chose to go into the 'Early Access' branch of Steam. ^_^

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.5.0 FPS Boost, Forging Table, New Music, Bug Fixes!
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.5.0[/h1]
[list][*]Implemented a whole new soundtrack
[*]Re-implemnted crop generation in the world
[*]Destroying a crop before it is finishing growing will now return you the original seed you planted
[*]Saved games now save your currently selected item slot
[*]Saved games now save your equipped items
[*]Added new biome: Small Pond
[*]Change all UI states to a single variable (lower the amount of variable comparisons each frame drastically)
[*]Different UIs can be switched seamlessly now. Stats to inventory to waypoint system, all without issues!
[*]Implemented forging table (90%), functional, just polishing the gui and interface
[*]Change terrain rendering over to surface based for a drastic increase in performance (Pre-rendered textures)
[*]Attempted to fix fatal error that everyone has been reporting
[*]Fixed bug: Compass crafting requirements were incorrect
[*]Fixed bug: Crops not dropping items correctly
[*]Fixed bug: Skeletons spawned when there is no water in the world caused crash
[*]Fixed bug: Game crash occasionally when planting crops
[*]Fixed bug: Ocean water and occasionally lake/pond water was not loaded after a game was saved for the first time
[*]Fixed bug: Lake/Pond water occasionally was moved out of place after the game was saved[/list]

[h1][b]Such Update, Very Wow[/b][/h1]
I know a lot of people were unhappy with the framerate they were getting. I completely understand and that's why I took the time to figure out a method to render the terrain more effeciently. If you care to read about how it works, read below!

I've implemented a whole new soundtrack. A musician friend of mine offered a couple tracks and so I am hoping to get some feedback from the community on it. I personally like the new music and find it far more fitting for the game than what I had before. Do let me know what you think though!

Now let's discuss the new crafting object, the forging table. This item must be placed in the world and used by first, clicking on it. This will bring up the brand new forge table UI. You put wood in the bottom left slot to fuel it and the required resource for what you wish to craft in the top left slot. Select the item you want and click the 'forge' button which will now have the name of the item you selected on it.

I'm hoping the table adds a bit more depth to the gameplay. I'm going to post an update shortly that will make the table craftable so you can get your hands on it!

[h1][b]How The New Terrain Rendering Works (For My Fellow Nerds)[/b][/h1]
To keep things short... We cache the terrain textures that should be on the screen into memory and render it as we normally would but as a single texture rather than looping through and drawing each tile individually. This provides a great fps boost since we aren't rendering each tile individually every frame. Instead we update the single texture with the new on-screen tiles only when it's needed.

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.4.6 Performance Improvements, Bug Fixes, And Music!
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.4.6[/h1]
[list][*]Implemented music (Sounds real nice)
[*]Plants now will break if they are on a surface they can't grow on
[*]Fixed bug: Player can walk on water
[*]Fixed bug: Equipping the carrying lantern crashes the game (Hot fixed)
[*]Fixed bug: Heavy sword doesn't do damage (Hot fixed)
[*]Fixed bug: Game crash occasionally when planting crops
[*]Made wood sword craftable
[*]Made light metal sword craftable
[*]Made disabled menus fade
[*]Lowered drop rate of corn and potato crops
[*]Improved rendering performance of sanity effects. Dark clouds surrounding sanity creatures and such
[*]Removed shadow quality option (Didn't do anything anyways)
[*]Removed anti-alias graphics option (Didn't do anything anyways besides negatively affect frame rate)
[*]Added new video option: vignette screen effect can now be toggled off in the graphics menu
[*]Added new video option: blood can now be toggled off in the graphics menu (50% implemented, the decals and effects are disabled by this option but death animations need to be changed still)[/list]

[h1][b]What's Special About This Update?[/b][/h1]
The biggest change you will probably notice is that I implemented music. Currently there are only two sound tracks but I plan on writing quite a few more within the next few weeks.

I've also switched the game back to the full code compilation (native code) to improve performance. After watching numerous game reviews with framerates as low as 20 and as high as 200, I was shocked. The performance loss is too drastic to drop support for the full compiler. I plan on further securing my code to ensure less crashes/bugs in the future. Please report any issues you have on the forums! ːCuteBearDollː

[h1][b]Community Requests[/b][/h1]
I fixed a couple bugs and implemented a few things that people have been requesting.

There were a few complaints that the main menu was confusing and that deselected menus should be indicated as such. I've added a fade on deselected menus to prevent confusion.

One user requested that blood can be toggled on/off. Whether this is to make the game child friendly or to help those who are hemophobic, it was an excellent suggestion!

I noticed a lot of people complaining about having a horrible framerate no matter what they do and realized the main issue was these people were playing on old GPUs or integrated graphics cards. I've made the vignette shader a video setting option that can be turned on or off. Switching it off may give you a massive framerate boost if you do not have a dedicated graphics card.

[h1][b]The New Calendar Page For Trello![/b][/h1]
If you are ever interested in what we are working on from a day to day basis, we've finally got around to making a calendar that we will be constantly updating as we push forward.

LINK HERE: [url=https://trello.com/b/eaw5bXk9/alpha-0-1/calendar]https://trello.com/b/eaw5bXk9/alpha-0-1/calendar[/url]

Thanks for reading everybody!

Hello everyone! I am officially flying out of Hawaii in just a few days and will be starting anew in Oregon! Why am I telling you this? I'm going to be out of commission for the next week or so (depending on delays) without a computer or internet.

Yours truly, Seabass... <3

notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.4.5[/h1]
[list][*]Made knives less delicious (Make all previously non-consumable items, not consumable again)
[*]Added new item: Frying Pan
[*]Added new item: Wooden Sword
[*]Added new item: Light Metal Sword
[*]Added new item: Heavy Metal Sword
[*]'Save Game' now only says, 'Save Game', instead of including the fix version
[*]Changed release version to interpreted code compilation

[h1][b]Why The Small Update?[/b][/h1]
I think it is rather important that you can't eat your entire inventory. It was a serious bug that I managed to over look and so I'm pushing this update NOW to avoid further confusion. In the meantime I've added swords just because I thought it would be nice to have a couple more weapons in the game. Like a frying pan. Why not? If we can have thousands of items/weapons in the game with the excellent foundation we've developed, why shouldn't we add everything we can think of?

I've also switched the release version to the much more stable interpreted code compilation. This should stop 99% of the bugs that have been getting reported. The result is a slightly lower framerate but I'd prefer a stable game with 200 fps than an unstable game with 400 fps.

I hope to hear what everyone thinks of this update below! ^_^

notes.title: What's To Come In The Next Update? Waypoints, Armor, And More!
notes.content:
[h1][b]What's Going On (Seabass)[/b][/h1]
As of recently I've felt like I have been slacking off and not working nearly enough on Project Explore. It's my goal to leave a mark on the Early Access community and to show that development doesn't have to be a slow process. I wanted to show people that we can push out updates every few days and pack them to the brim with new content. I don't feel like I've been meeting my own standard recently and so this update is my shot at self redemption. I hope you like what we've got done and can hopefully give me some feedback on it. Enjoy all the pictures!

[h1][b]Bug Fixes Of Course![/b][/h1]
There is a list of bugs I've fixed which can be seen [url=https://trello.com/b/eaw5bXk9/alpha-0-1]HERE[/url].
The biggest fix being the issue of kills not counting towards Steam statistics.

[h1][b]New Achievments[/b][/h1]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/CvCIUZV.png[/img][img]http://i.imgur.com/wOcjU0H.png[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/9nZJGHn.png[/img][img]http://i.imgur.com/xMOffWl.png[/img]
Now you can feel better about killing off this already deteriorating tribe.


[h1][b]New Waypoint System[/b][/h1]

Place a flag, and then set it's name.
[img]http://i.imgur.com/XUbFvqN.png[/img]

Press 'ENTER' and the flag is now named, 'Waypoint 1'.
[img]http://i.imgur.com/LIo744X.png[/img]

Equip the compass and 'RIGHT CLICK', choose a waypoint to point towards.
[img]http://i.imgur.com/OFlRXXQ.png[/img]

Your compass will now point towards that waypoint.
[img]http://i.imgur.com/DVGwtt6.png[/img]

This is a feature that I know a lot of people wanted and needed. There is no limit to how many waypoints there are. I'll be changing the model for the waypoint as well before the official release of 0.1.4.1.

[h1][b]Wearable Armor/Clothing[/b][/h1]

Here is a tiny image to show you what this means.
[img]http://i.imgur.com/Tzri24s.png[/img]

You can now equip armor that will increase your resistance to damage. We're still adding a few more things to it before we release it but you can expect to see it in version 0.1.4.1 (the next update). Now finding your way back home will be breeze!

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.4.0 Bug Fixes, Combat System Re-Work, And Some Balancing! Youtube Permission!
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.4.0[/h1]
[b]Game Balancing:[/b]
[list][*]Adjusted the spawn rate of rocks and metal. (Increased spawn rate)
[*]Adjusted damage variables to be more realisitic
[*]NPCs now have armor and knockback resistance
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]
[list][*]Fixed Bug: Perk slot text display had various issues
[*]Fixed Bug: Achievement 'Get Baked!' now works!
[*]Fixed Bug: Achievement 'Rock On!' now works!
[*]Fixed Bug: Achievement 'Deforestation' now works!
[*]Fixed Bug: Achievement 'Heavy Metal' now works!
[*]Fixed Bug: Achievement 'Screw you Mother Nature' now works!
[*]Fixed Bug: Stat 'Trees Cut' now works!
[*]Fixed Bug: Stat 'Rocks Cut' now works!
[*]Fixed Bug: Skeletons spawning in bodies of water
[*]Fixed Bug: Pillar sprite was off centered
[/list]
[b]Community Requests:[/b]
[list][*]Flipped the axe [url=Flipped the axe http://strawpoll.me/4171401]http://strawpoll.me/4171401[/url]
[/list]
[b]Optimizations/Re-Works:[/b]
[list][*]Re-write of the weapon damage and effect handling system
[*]Re-write of the AI damage system
[*]Re-write of the knockback system
[*]Removed Items: Dull Knife, Sharp Knife
[/list]

[h1]Seabass Talks About This Update[/h1]
This update will officially fix the issues regarding recently added achievements. It also fixes the balancing issue of never seeing rocks in the world. I tried to balance the spawn rate this time around.

Spike noticed my glued together weapon and damage system, and suggested that I re-write the whole thing to be more modular. He had a good point, the previous system required about 15 minutes of my time to implement a new weapon which is just absurd. Unfortunately I just never had time to re-write the entire system because I was so focused on pushing content every update rather than fixing behind the scene issues.

After about 12 hours of work on it I managed to write a much better system for weapon/knockback related code. It runs better (although you will not notice it) and takes only a moment for me to add new weapons now. I was also able to work in damage and knockback resistance. Each NPC is unique and we have plans to expand on the system for players as well. This will include wearable clothing such as armor and helmets (NOT HATS).

[h1]What To Expect In The Near Future[/h1]
I have plans to work on the compass and expand it as more of feature than an item. We have plans of implementing a waypoint type system for navigating with it. You'll see it in game soon enough.

Hopefully I will be able to implement the armor system by the time the next update rolls around. We'll just have to wait and see though.

[h1]Youtube Permission[/h1]
If you wish to do any youtube videos for Project Explore, I give explicit permission to do so with monetization on your video. I've received a lot of emails on this matter and so I'd just like to clear it up once and for all. I see nothing wrong with earning money by playing a game and having an audience watch. I could care less to be honest. I personally love and support anyone who takes time out of their day to record and edit a video that promotes a game. Especially an indie game.

Well thanks for reading and as always... We couldn't come this far without your support! So thank you for making a dream come true!

notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.3.7[/h1]
[b]New Art:[/b]
[list][*]Replaced Item Art: Dr Salt
[*]Replaced Item Art: Soda
[*]Replaced Item Art: PepD
[*]Replaced Item Art: Vitamin Water
[*]Replaced Item Art: Veggie Water
[*]Replaced Item Art: Water Bottle
[*]Replaced Item Art: Cloth
[*]Replaced Item Art: Animal Fat
[*]Replaced Item Art: Stick
[*]Replaced Item Art: Wood
[*]Replaced Item Art: Camp Fire
[*]Replaced Item Art: Big Fire[/list]
[b]New Items:[/b]
[list]
[*]Added New Item: Empty Bottle
[/list]
[b]New Implementations:[/b]
[list]
[*]Implemented refillable bottles
[*]Implemented multiple step chunk loading to reduce frame dipping
[/list]
[b]Bug Fixes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed Bug: Fire sound keeps playing even after the rain puts the fire out
[*]Fixed Bug: Some roof tops not becoming transparent
[*]Fixed Bug: Game crashes due to order of execution of certain scripts such as fishing and using the shovel
[*]Fixed Bug: Pausing and resuming the game would activate a 5x5 chunk area instead of the 3x3 chunk default
[*]Fixed Bug: Skeletons spawning on water
[/list]
[b]Misc Changes:[/b]
[list]
[*]Made non constructed doors unbreakable via the hammer
[*]Lowered skeleton loot spawnrate
[*]Renamed Item 'Soda' to 'Nymph'
[/list]


[h1]Developer Comments On This Update[/h1]
Refillable water bottles seemed like a cool feature to add (thanks to idiotekque for the idea) and so I worked it in. While implementing it I found tons of strange bugs in the way the world was loading and fixed the order the code was executing in hope of fixing these issues. The changes I made appear successful and while I was doing that I worked in multi-step chunk loading. What is 'multi-step chunk loading' you ask? It just means instead of loading 3x3 chunks in 1 frame, I separate the process into 1 chunk per frame. When you are walking by massive houses in multiplayer, this will be much more appreciated.

I worked on fixing a few more bugs and polishing the overall experience. I think that the game is feeling a lot more stable as of this update. I fixed the roof top issue and the fire sound that would NEVER stop playing when it rained. It was quite annoying to hear the calming crackle of a fire in the distance while it clearly was unlit. I don't know if I'm just picky but it bothered me. Thank you everyone who has been reporting bugs!

Idiotekque has started his work on replacing the item art of every item in the game. It is taking a bit because we really want them to look good and come out clean this time around.


[h1]Answering Fan Mail Regarding Steam Workshop Changes[/h1]
A lot of discussion is going around regarding the changes to the Steam Workshop and I just want everyone to know that they (Valve) are really looking into it. Check out Reddit for example, Gabe himself was on there answering people. So don't panic just yet. This is a good thing for the Steam community!

Now I must answer the question, no I do not plan on adding the Steam workshop to Project Explore, at least not while we are in Early Access. If I update the game and it breaks a ton of mods, well then a bunch of mod creators have a lot of angry customers. Sorry but I am not going to encourage building mods on a game that updates every few days.

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.3.6[/h1]

[*]Made Object Craftable: Wood Table

[/list]

[h1]About This Update[/h1]
I am working hard to add more furniture and ways to decorate your home. It might seem like a weird direction to go but I think it adds more depth to the game as well as a bit more of an end game. The table can be used to display items you put on it which I think is pretty cool.

I've finally got around to adding outlines to text which makes them much easier to read. It has been requested quite a few times and I just didn't really get around to it until now.

Idiotekque is working on drawing new art for all the items I originally did. Unfortunately I'm not an artist and I did a horrid job on drawing up art for the items. You'll notice he has drawn up new art for the crafting tabs and it looks much better compared to it's previuos art. These changes will continue to come.

[h1]The Development Process[/h1]
I think it is important to communicate with everyone how things are going on our side of life. I'm still working my job although I cut back a bit on those hours so that I could spend a little more time at home working on this as well as spending time with m'lady and friends. It's important to relax and let ideas roll around in your head before spending hours implementing them. It's also important to not work more than you can handle. I learned this pretty quickly when I first released Project Explore. 

I would wake up, work, go to my job, come home, work, go to sleep, and repeat. It was like this for a few weeks and really has taken it's toll on me. We are not a studio, we are not a company, 'we' are a developer and an artist. I will continue to push updates as I have and will work my hardest to provide high quality content on a regular basis.

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.3.5 New Biome, New AI, And Major Optimizations
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS. [/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.3.5[/h1]
[list][*]Particles are now cleared from memory manually, this might fix the game crashing when being closed (High Priority)
[*]Added New Texture: Mossy Stone
[*]Added New Texture: Dry Dirt
[*]Added New Object: Pillar (Ruins)
[*]Added New Biome: Ruins
[*]Decals are now deleted when moved off screen
[*]Fixed window re-adjusting when starting a new world, instead it just re-centers
[*]Fixed death animations, they can actually be seen now
[*]Changed the way terrain is rendered. It looks a little different now but it comes with a massive performance increase
[*]Optimized terrain transitions
[*]Changed items to spawn around dead NPCs instead of on top of them
[*]Graves now despawn
[*]Added New AI: Nomad Stalker
[*]Added New AI: Nomad Ripper
[*]NPCs now will try not to group up into one spot (they will not get stuck inside of each other)
[*]Implemented new customization options
[*]Changed the way the player is rendered (re-layered)[/list]

[h1][b]A Few Words From The Lead Developer (Seabass)[/b][/h1]
I spent a while on the new AI and a few optimizations. There have been many complaints about the framerate dropping over time and I have spent a lot of time to address that issue. I recommend starting a new game to actually take advantage of some of the changes I've made in this update. I am getting about 100 frames higher on average now that I've re-worked the terrain rendering system. Quite an improvement but I'm sure there is still room for further optimization. I finally added code to remove graves over time. Decals are deleted a bit more often now as well.

Another complaint I've seen a lot (even in reviews) is that there is not a ton of content. Idiotekque and I decided on our next approach to developing the game and have implemented it in this update. I think everyone will be pleasantly surprised when they find the new content. It did take us a couple of days and some serious crunch time but we made it within the 5 day mark (by 15 minutes).

It was worth buckling down and getting through it to keep our promise to everyone that there will be an update every 3-5 days. I do not lie (at least I don't try to :P). It was a pain writing the code for some of the new AI and figuring out how I would fix the framerate outside of obvious issues.

I expect everyone will enjoy this update and what it brings. Thanks for supporting an indie developer. ːCuteBearDollː

[h1][b]A Few Words From The Artist (Idiotekque)[/b][/h1]
Hey guys! It's been a little while since our last update, but I do think it's been worth the wait. We've been listening to your feedback, and while we obviously can't cover all the suggestions quickly, something we have done in this update is take that feedback and let it work to prioritize what we've already been working on.

A piece of feedback that I really agreed with and set to addressing ASAP was the complaint that the difficulty of the game is very lacking. Basically you can start the game off with a rock and kill every enemy in the game with relative ease. That's silly, but sadly it's been necessary so that a character doesn't just start up the game and get murdered immediately. This update, however, is going to be a nice step forward in addressing that issue.

We've added a new biome, for starters. The environment needed some variety, so that was an immediate priority. With the biome will come new enemies. I'm not going to spoil anything, because you'll have to explore in game to find what I'm talking about, but what you'll find is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the direction we're heading in. Be prepared for some tougher battles!

In addition to that, I've also expanded the ever-increasing library of character customization parts with some new hairstyles and a new shirt type. More will come, so hopefully there will be something for everyone.

That's all from me. Hope you all enjoy the new biome and what it brings!

[h1][b]Check Out The New Update! Here Is A Video![/b][/h1]
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DARfQdjXuCA]Update Gameplay Video By CalmDownLevelUp[/url]

I recommend starting a new game to actually take advantage of some of the changes I've made in this update. I am getting about 100 frames higher on average now that I've re-worked the terrain rendering system. Quite an improvement but I'm sure there is still room for further optimization. I finally added code to remove graves over time. Decals are deleted a bit more often now as well.

Another complaint I've seen a lot (even in reviews) is that there is not a ton of content. Idiotekque and I decided on our next approach to developing the game and have implemented it in this update. I think everyone will be pleasantly surprised when they find the new content. It did take us a couple of days and some serious crunch time but we made it within the 5 day mark (by 15 minutes).

It was worth buckling down and getting through it to keep our promise to everyone that there will be an update every 3-5 days. I do not lie (at least I don't try to :P). It was a pain writing the code for some of the new AI and figuring out how I would fix the framerate outside of obvious issues.

I expect everyone will enjoy this update and what it brings. Thanks for supporting an indie developer. :CuteBearDoll:

[h1][b]A Few Words From The Artist (Idiotekque)[/b][/h1]
Hey guys! It's been a little while since our last update, but I do think it's been worth the wait. We've been listening to your feedback, and while we obviously can't cover all the suggestions quickly, something we have done in this update is take that feedback and let it work to prioritize what we've already been working on.

A piece of feedback that I really agreed with and set to addressing ASAP was the complaint that the difficulty of the game is very lacking. Basically you can start the game off with a rock and kill every enemy in the game with relative ease. That's silly, but sadly it's been necessary so that a character doesn't just start up the game and get murdered immediately. This update, however, is going to be a nice step forward in addressing that issue.

We've added a new biome, for starters. The environment needed some variety, so that was an immediate priority. With the biome will come new enemies. I'm not going to spoil anything, because you'll have to explore in game to find what I'm talking about, but what you'll find is just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to the direction we're heading in. Be prepared for some tougher battles!

In addition to that, I've also expanded the ever-increasing library of character customization parts with some new hairstyles and a new shirt type. More will come, so hopefully there will be something for everyone.

That's all from me. Hope you all enjoy the new biome and what it brings!

[h1][b]Check Out The New Update! Here Is A Video![/b][/h1]
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DARfQdjXuCA]Update Gameplay Video By CalmDownLevelUp[/url]

notes.title: What We Are Working On Right Now And My Public Answer To The Pay To Play Suggestions
notes.content:
[h1][b]This Update Might Take A Little Longer[/b][/h1]

While the artist finishes up work on some new NPCs, I've been hard at work doing a couple things. First off I got a bit done for the multiplayer side, pretty much I got a bit more functionally built into the master server. It now can read data from public servers and decide when that server has gone down. It partially works with the client to send the full server list although there is a bug in the system right now I'm still ironing out.

I implemented a few new textures for the biomes and created a new pillar object as well. I am also beginning work on the new NPCs which may take a little bit as they do not behave like the animals do. I'm trying to say all this without spoiling anything of course so it's quite difficult to be specific. I should have these new NPCs implemented within the next few days.

I will post version 0.1.3.5 once they are functional and the new biome is working well.

[h1][b]News On The Overall Development Process[/b][/h1]

I'm happy to say that I am still loving the development process and it has yet to become a chore. With that said you can expect a lot more content and continuous improvements. I'm glad to see that the community is really doing well and remains very supportive. I couldn't ask for more.

The artist and I are getting more comfortable working as a team (something I'm horrible at) which can only lead to higher quality work from the two of us.

[h1][b]Answering The Pay To Play Suggestions[/b][/h1]

Many people have contacted me and have suggested making the singleplayer feature free (essentially the game) but requiring a purchase to play the multiplayer. My answer to that is simply no. I would feel like I'm cheating people out of something. Maybe I'm just too old fashion but I believe in purchasing a product once and getting everything that product entails. Including and not limited to future updates, bug fixes, and additional content.

Imagine if you loved the singleplayer and then paid for the multiplayer and disliked it. Wouldn't you feel like you were cheated? I would. Compare that to this... You buy the game and love the singleplayer. You try out the multiplayer and dislike it. Maybe multiplayer just doesn't feel right to you but you loved the singleplayer, at least you didn't spend your money on a specific feature just to regret that decision shortly after.

Please share your opinion on this matter. Perhaps I'm wrong and not seeing the potential of this idea. I'd love to discuss it.

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.3.4 New Achievements, Bug Fixes, And Bleeding!
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS. [/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.3.4[/h1]
[list][*]Added bleeding status
[*]Changed temperature to food loss equation based on polynomial data
[*]Player and AI when spawning, now will move to avoid being stuck in a solid object
[*]Increased bleed time
[*]Player loses health when bleeding, -0.01
[*]Added world deletion (Windows Only)
[*]Fixed issue with save files adding additional '.sav' onto file each time it was saved
[*]Fixed Bug: Dashing with the shovel equipped gets the player stuck until item is changed
[*]Made sand tile allow floor placement
[*]Made wet sand tile allow floor placement
[*]Added player bleeding status when saving the world
[*]Added New Stat: Trees cut
[*]Added New Stat: Rocks broke
[*]Added New Achievement: Get Baked
[*]Added new achievement: Rock On!
[*]Added New Achievement: Screw You Mother Nature
[*]Added New Achievement: Deforestation
[*]Added New Achievement: Heavy Metal
[*]Fixed Bug: World loading on the edge of the map seems to repeat itself and cause massive performance issues
[*]Fixed gap between the fishing line and the fishing pole when fishing
[*]Added New Item: Bandage
[*]Made bandage craftable
[*]Made another attempt to fix the player getting pushed off the map
[*]Stopped some objects from being drawn when there is a ceiling blocking it (Light sources and particle emitters)
[/list]


[h1][b]About This Update[/b][/h1]
I spent some time on starting to add more long term achievements. Achievements are an awesome way of saying 'Thank you for playing'.

Bleeding has only been a cosmetic effect until now. You will see a status popup when you are bleeding. It can be life threatening so it is vital to your survival to carry at least one bandage on you at all times.

I've changed the temperature to calorie loss system to a polynomial equation (thanks to some helpers on my live stream). It's basically a big beautiful curve instead of a bunch of conditional statements.

There was a bug where the world would keep generating the same chunks off the screen and it was causing horrible lag issues even after a short period of time. The system now checks to see if it is off of the screen before generating the chunk.

A lot of people requested a way to delete saved games, I've added that. Right click the file you want to delete. It will prompt you with a 'are you sure' type message. I could not find a way to implement it for Linux yet but seeing that it only supports one world at a time regardless, it doesn't seem like a huge issue.

Certain lights (campfires, lantern) are no longer rendered when they are indoors and the player is not. This improves performance and will hopefully improve the future multiplayer experience.

The player and the AI will now check for objects when they spawn to make sure they do not spawn directly into a rock or wall. Animals are still spawning inside of houses but I'm working on it. I have to do a lot of playing around with the world generation script (thousands of lines of code) to fix that issue so it should be in the next update.

You may have noticed that there is not a lot of new content in this update. I'd like to say sorry in advance. I'm still waiting on our artist to get more done for the new biome we have planned. It'll be worth the wait though. New AI is planned as well as new structures for the biome. Spriting does take time though and he is working very hard on it. In the meantime I am doing all I can to fix current issues with the game as well as add additional features/content.

Thank you for reading and please report any bugs you experience. I'll do my best to address any issues as soon as I'm available.

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.3.3 Character Customization, Save System Fix, And Audio Fix Up!
notes.content:
[b]SAVES WILL NOT WORK BETWEEN PREVIOUS VERSIONS AND THIS ONE[/b]

You guys are going to really like this update. Some may be mad about the save games being broken again but trust me, it was worth it. I'll explain more after the patch notes.

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.3.3[/h1]
[list][*]Fixed bug: Putting away the fishing rod while fishing will leave the line in the water and allow you to catch fish
[*]Fixed memory leak in file loading ds_list
[*]Added Character Customization Menu
[*]Implemented Character Customization System
[*]Re-worked player rendering system
[*]Fixed Bug: Decal system saves decals by sprite index, changed to asset_index
[*]Added water to collision checking when being knocked back
[*]Adjusted sound positioning and falloff for footsteps, impacts, and weapon swings
[*]Fixed Bug: Rain not playing audio when reloading
[*]Changed audio for ambient noise (Sounds a lot better)
[*]Added Idiotekque to the credits (the artist)
[*](Linux) Removed pop-up message when saving[/list]

[h1][b]Words From The Developer[/b][/h1]
This update fixes tons of major issues. I'll explain...

1. We replaced the horrible player art I had originally drawn up.

2. There is finally character customization (thanks to Idiotekque).

3. The save system is finally bullet proof. I had completely overlooked the fact that the decals were still saved by their real (their number) index instead of their string (name) index. This meant if I added a new sprite it would break the save system each time. That is now fixed entirely.

4. The audio has been fixed up and balanced a lot. I played the game for about 10 seconds and my ears were bleeding from the lack of balance in volume. I would hit a tree and my ear drums would explode. I spent a good 3 hours trying to balance the audio. I even modified specific features of some of the sounds such as the bass and treble. The footsteps of animals now is distanced correctly and sounds a lot more realistic. The players footsteps are much more diminished. Overall the game feels and sounds a lot better now.

I think everyone will get a lot closer to seeing what I've envisioned for the game now that we've fixed a lot of the outstanding issues. I will be posting a new trailer soon as well to show off how much progress the game has made.

Thanks for reading and as always, thank you for the support. ^_^

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.3.2 Tooltips, Better Rain, Beautiful Sounds, And A Few Words From The Developers.
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS. [/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.3.2[/h1]
[list][*]Replaced door texture, now more visible
[*]Added new item: The Tom Hank Redemption
[*]Added new item: The Godmother
[*]Added new item: 28 Days Prior
[*]Added new item: Above Average Hero 6
[*]Right clicking with mouse now goes back in the main menu
[*]Implemented new fire sound for both the small and large fire
[*]Added New Animal: Doe
[*]Updated art for 'How To Not Go Crazy' in-game and on the achievement "How To Not Go Crazy"
[*]Updated art for compass in-game and on the achievement "Novice Navigator"
[*]Took wolf out of spawn area (accidentally left it in in the previous version)
[*]Fixed rain drops spawning inside of each other (It may now seem to be twice as many rain drops)
[*]Audio now pauses and resumes when pausing the game
[*]Audio now will stop playing when you quit to the main menu
[*]Optimized rain drops (only checks for roof collision when first created)
[*]Rain drops are more transparent when hitting roofs
[*]Rain drops always make a splash effect now
[*]Implemented new rain sound
[*]Added achievement: 28 Days Prior
[*]Replaced small crate sprite
[*]Added new item: The Silence of the Goats
[*]Added new item: Raiders of the Old Park
[*]Added object interaction click sound
[*]Fixed bug where animals are able to hit player out of world
[*]Fixed bug where player can hit animals out of the world
[*]Replaced sprite for 'Tale of Two Girls And Thy Cup'
[*]Changed item: 'Tail of Two Girls and Thy Cup' to 'Tale of Two Maidens and Thy Chalice'
[*]Fixed inventory crafting buttons, mouse can no longer hover over two buttons at the same time
[*]Optimized 'mouse over' script
[*]Now when the player is hit, the inventory closes
[*]Implemented tooltip to display item names in crafting menu when the mouse is over it (ingredients)
[*]Adjusted red flash when taking damage
[/list]

[h1][b]What's Coming Next (Seabass, Creator/Lead Developer)[/b][/h1]
I'm hoping to start taking some steps into improving the immersion of the game. Feeling like you really are the character is important for any game. A few things I've tried to start out with include the fire sound effect and the rain sound. Even if they are small changes they do make a difference.

A lot of people seem to be facing the main issue of, "There isn't enough content". I'd like you to know that we are aware of the concerns and complaints of the community. I would love to add more content and create more variety in the world. Believe me when I say that we are working on it. Unfortunately I do have a day job that I have to attend to ([i]"Work sucks, I know" -Blink 182[/i]) and it takes up about 30 hours of my week currently.

I'm hoping that sooner than later I can make developing this game my #1 and only priority.

I want to thank everyone who has provided feedback and suggestions for Project Explore. Without you the game wouldn't be where it is now.

[h1][b]What's Coming Next (Idiotekque)[/b][/h1]
The grind to bring a lot of current art in the game up to snuff has been a continual process, and it will keep up as I replace a lot of the item art that needs replacing. Now that the first handful of creatures is done, however, you should all be seeing some NEW content in the game in the not so distant future. Before then, the player sprite is getting a much needed rework, and it pretty much is good to go as soon as we get the character customization menu in working order.

Yes, you heard right: Character customization.

When I started working on the new sprite, I couldn't help but feel like breaking the pieces apart, adding new pieces, and just rolling with it was the best direction to go. This is definitely going to be vital when multiplayer is integrated down the road so that everyone doesn't look like clones as well. Granted the pieces you'll be able to use will be relatively limited, but more will come, so no worries about lack of variety there.

I'm gonna start putting together some brand new enemies soon as well, as well as trying to bring a whole new aspect to the game as far as... the feel goes. The reason to things, why you're in the middle of nowhere, and where you really are, and what's there beyond just a bunch of ravenous beasts. It's gonna be cool. It's also gonna be a lot of work and take time, so I'll leave you all with that thought.

Enjoy the update,
Idiotekque

[list][*]Brand new character sprite
[*]Character customization (Limited)
[*]New enemies
[*]New weapons
[*]Continually updated item sprites
[*]Secret stuff I'm not going to tell you
[/list]

notes.title: Update Version 0.1.3.0 The Start Of A Great Journey
notes.content:
[b]SAVES MAY NOT WORK BETWEEN THIS AND PREVIOUS VERSIONS. PLEASE DO NOT POST BUGS THAT ARE DUE TO LOADING SAVES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS.[/b]

[h1]Changes In Version 0.1.3.0[/h1]
[list][*]Added in-game text boxes for input. You can copy, paste, use the mouse, everything you can do with a normal text box.
[*]Changed load menu, now gives you a list of every save in the game folder. You can scroll through it with the mouse wheel

[*]Rain drops now properly check for roofs and change alpha accordingly
[*]All light sources now start disabled when first placed. You may not want another player to see you as you put down a lantern for example
[*]When raining, fires are put out if they are not under a ceiling of some sort
[*]Fires can not be started if they are in the rain

[*]Fixed rain hitting constructed roof that may have led to a crash due to a missing variable
[*]Re-worked menu music
[*]Fine tuned a few sounds (volume)
[*]Increased damage done to bucks with arrows (-50 HP)
[*]Changed code used in the chunk system, keeps more chunks active
[*]Changed stick crafting, 1 log gives 2 sticks
[*]Fixed Project Explore (All the games programming) to work correctly with the latest stable version of Game Maker: Studio, Version 1.4.1567

[b]What's To Come[/b]
Project Explore has come a far way since it's original release into early access. I'm happy to say that the game is doing great so far and I can almost guarantee Project Explore to be complete by this time next year. I plan to leave my day job in a few months and focus all my time, and energy into Project Explore.

Everyone in the community has been very helpful in the development process with great suggestions and motivational support. I could not have ever imagined that the game would grow to this size and be so well received. I am left speechless everytime I open the store page to see the reviews at "Very Positive".
